data.title: Ixigo Swings To Rs 63 Crore Profit In Q2
data.description:
Travel booking platform ixigo reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year earlier, helped by a partial stake sale in Freshbus and rapid growth in hotel bookings.

Revenue from operations rose 13 per cent year-on-year to Rs 320.96 crore in the second quarter of FY27, from Rs 284.23 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a regulatory filing by Le Travenues Technology, which operates ixigo.

Total expenses increased to Rs 309.51 crore from Rs 291.89 crore a year earlier.

The company reported quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued growth in its travel booking business.

Hotels was ixigo's fastest-growing business segment by GTV, with the metric rising 159 per cent year-on-year to Rs 111.34 crore. The September quarter marked the first time the company reported hotels as a separate business line.

In a joint statement, ixigo Group Chief Executive Officer Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar and Group Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Devendra Singh said the company had recorded its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax, aided by the partial sale of its stake in Freshbus.

The executives said the company would continue investing in hotels and artificial intelligence as key drivers of its long-term growth.

data.title: GPT Infraprojects Secures Rs 134 Cr Western Railway Signalling Contract
data.description:
The project covers four railway sections in Ratlam division, with completion scheduled within 548 days from the appointed date

GPT Infraprojects has secured a railway signalling contract worth Rs 134.11 crore, including GST, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Alcon Builders and Engineers Private Limited, the company said in a stock exchange filing.

The order has been awarded by the Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer, Western Railway, Ratlam Division, with the contract valued at Rs 113.65 crore excluding GST. The project covers signalling works across multiple double-line railway sections under the Ratlam division.

The scope includes survey, design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of 4-Aspect Automatic Block Signalling with electronic interlocking and dual multi-section digital axle counters at auto huts. The contract also covers associated alterations to electronic interlocking systems at stations.

The works will be executed across the Nagda-Ujjain-Tajpur, Phanda-Sant Hirdaram Nagar, Ujjain-Karchha and Mangliyagaon-Indore double-line sections. GPT Infraprojects said the project is scheduled for completion within 548 days from the appointed date.

With the latest contract, GPT Infraprojects' net outstanding order book has reached Rs 5,651 crore. The company has recorded total order inflow of Rs 1,478 crore so far in fiscal 2027, strengthening its project pipeline for the year.

GPT Infraprojects operates through infrastructure and sleeper segments, with its infrastructure business covering civil and railway projects. Its activities include bridges, road-over-bridges and railway signalling works, alongside concrete sleeper manufacturing.

Railway Business Gains

The company manufactures concrete sleepers for railway projects through facilities in West Bengal, South Africa, Namibia and Ghana. Its operations therefore span both infrastructure execution and railway component manufacturing across India and overseas markets.

Shares of GPT Infraprojects ended nearly 1 per cent higher on the day. The stock has gained around 15 per cent so far this year, as the company continues to build its order pipeline across railway and infrastructure projects.

data.title: RailTel Secures Rs 186.5 Cr Orders For Recruitment, Cybersecurity
data.description:
The larger project runs through 2031 for railway recruitment services, while the second covers technology and cybersecurity support through 2029

RailTel Corporation of India has secured two work orders worth a combined Rs 186.51 crore, including a Rs 167.52 crore contract from the Railway Recruitment Board (RRB), Secunderabad, for recruitment examination services.

The company received both orders on 16 October, according to its regulatory filing. The contracts cover recruitment examination management as well as IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions, further adding to RailTel's project pipeline.

The larger order, estimated at Rs 167.52 crore excluding taxes, covers AM-RMS services for the pre-examination and post-examination stages of RRB recruitment conducted through various Centralised Employment Notifications (CENs).

The contract is scheduled to remain valid until 15 October 2031, giving RailTel a long-term engagement to provide services associated with the recruitment examination process conducted by the railway recruitment board.

IT Infrastructure Order

The second order, worth Rs 18.99 crore including taxes, has been awarded by Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions. The three-year contract is scheduled to run until 16 October 2029, expanding RailTel's recent project wins across technology, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity-related services.

The latest contracts follow several orders secured by RailTel in recent months, covering digital governance, telecom infrastructure and technology services for government and public-sector clients.

On 13 October, RailTel received a Rs 49 crore order, including taxes, from the Odisha government's Higher Education Department to develop 83 digital application modules under a Comprehensive Digital Governance Platform.

In August, the company secured a Rs 165 crore contract, including taxes, from Western Coalfields to establish a Multiprotocol Label Switching Virtual Private Network on a rental basis for 60 months.

The Western Coalfields contract is scheduled to continue until 20 September 2031. RailTel also received a Rs 166.8 crore order from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation in August to extend an existing Infrastructure-as-a-Service arrangement through RailTel by one year.

The EPFO contract includes additional components and is scheduled to run until 9 February 2027. RailTel shares closed at Rs 255.05 on the BSE on 16 October, rising 0.57 per cent during the session.

data.title: Nifty soars 2.8% this week: What lies ahead for Dalal Street? - Experts decode 5 triggers, key levels for next week
data.description:
Stock Market Outlook, Oct. 17 -- Indian equities staged a strong comeback this week, with the Nifty 50 rising 2.77% and the Sensex surging 3.11%, as renewed buying in information technology (IT) stocks, easing global bond-yield pressures and resilient domestic institutional inflows lifted investor sentiment.

Both benchmarks also extended their gains for a second consecutive session on Friday, strengthening hopes of a recovery after the recent market correction.

On Friday, the Sensex climbed 413.66 points, or 0.56%, to close at 74,729.27 on Friday, while the Nifty advanced 148.80 points, or 0.65%, to settle at 23,146.15. For the week, the Sensex gained 2,256.94 points, while the Nifty added 625.7 points.

However, the rally faces several tests, including whether earnings growth broadens beyond IT, foreign investor selling eases further and the Nifty breaks through immediate resistance. Market experts believe investors should remain selective as global macroeconomic uncertainty and domestic inflation concerns persist.

The September-quarter earnings season will remain a major driver of market sentiment. Investors will assess whether companies can deliver stronger revenue growth and margins across banking, consumption and industrials, rather than relying primarily on IT stocks to sustain the recovery.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments Limited, said, "The sustainability of the recovery will hinge on earnings growth broadening beyond IT, with revenue and margin delivery across financials, consumption and industrials under close scrutiny."

Foreign institutional investor (FII) flows remain a key variable for the market. While foreign portfolio outflows have moderated, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continue to provide support through sustained buying.

Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services Ltd, said weekly foreign portfolio outflows narrowed to Rs.8,991 crore, while domestic institutional investors purchased approximately Rs.7,813 crore worth of shares. Any further moderation in foreign selling could help stabilise the indices.

Global monetary policy expectations, geopolitical developments and energy prices will remain important determinants of investor appetite for equities. Higher crude prices can fuel inflation, while rising bond yields may increase the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investments and put pressure on equity valuations.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking. noted, "Global markets are currently in a transition phase. Major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, have started moving towards an easier monetary policy stance, while growth remains subdued across regions such as Europe and China."

IT shares have been a key driver of the recent recovery, supported by a shift in global investor positioning following a sell-off in international AI and semiconductor stocks. Singh attributed the buying interest in Indian IT services companies to concerns over elevated valuations and delayed monetisation cycles among global AI hardware and chipmakers.

Indian IT companies, with their established execution capabilities and comparatively attractive valuations, have benefited from this rotation. Investors will watch whether the momentum continues or broadens to other sectors.

The Nifty has rebounded from support near 22,200 and reclaimed its 21-day exponential moving average (EMA) around 22,900, indicating improving near-term momentum. However, the index must overcome immediate resistance to extend its recovery.

Singh said, "As long as Nifty sustains above this level, buying interest is likely to persist, making a buy-on-dips strategy prudent. On the upside, the 55-day EMA near 23360 remains the immediate resistance."

The near-term technical setup has improved, but experts favour selective stock picking over aggressive index-level positioning.

The Nifty's immediate resistance is around 23,360, corresponding to its 55-day EMA. A decisive breakout could open the way towards 23,600, according to Singh's technical assessment. On the downside, the 21-day EMA near 22,900 is an important level to defend, while 22,200 remains a significant support zone.

Mishra's medium-term assessment is constructive, subject to an improvement in corporate earnings. The analyst said, "Immediate resistance sits near 23,800-24,000; a sustained breakout above that could set up a retest of the 26,350-26,500 zone over 6 months, contingent on earnings acceleration."

The analyst identified 23,000 as immediate support, followed by the 52-week low near 22,182. These are medium-term levels and should be distinguished from the nearer-term technical markers highlighted by Singh.

For investors, a staggered buy-on-dips approach may be preferable to chasing sharp rallies, provided key support levels hold. Companies with sustainable earnings growth, strong balance sheets and reasonable valuations are likely to offer a more disciplined route through continued volatility.

India's October PMI, US jobless claims, Japan's inflation data, Corporate earnings and management commentary, rupee, crude oil bond yields, and FII and DII activity will be closely watched next week.

Nair cautioned that the market was likely to remain selective and earnings-driven amid elevated inflation and a tightening policy bias. The next leg of the rally will depend on whether corporate earnings support current valuations and the Nifty can clear resistance while holding its recently reclaimed support levels.

data.title: Kennedy, White House officials to revive food policy talks next week: Politico
data.description:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is expected to meet with senior White House officials next week to discuss the status of U.S. food policy as part of a revived push to define ultra-processed foods, Politico reported on Saturday.

Discussions among officials have gathered pace over recent weeks after a pause this summer, according to three Trump administration officials who were granted anonymity to disclose internal conversations.

Previously, Kennedy promised to get a definition for ultra-processed foods “by April” and follow up with a system for food grading in a move that could tighten regulation on packaged offerings such as chips and sodas.

In August, the HHS and the U.S. Department of Agriculture submitted the federal government’s first proposed definition of ultra-processed foods for final review as a white paper, which, however, fell short of being a legally enforceable rule.

The discussions come less than two weeks into the midterm elections amid calls by Kennedy and many members of his Make America Healthy Again movement to include warning labels for ultra-processed foods.

HHS didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

Potentially relevant tickers: PepsiCo , Kellanova (K), Kraft Heinz , McDonald's , Yum! Brands , Restaurant Brands International , Coca-Cola , B&G Foods , Conagra Brands , Celsius , Hershey , Mondelez , and  Invesco Food & Beverage ETF

data.title: IDBI Bank Q2 profit falls 39% on high base, underlying earnings rise 14%
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- IDBI Bank reported a 39 per cent year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 2,205 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, largely due to a one-time gain recorded last year, while its underlying profit grew 14 per cent amid stronger interest income and improving asset quality.

According to the bank's earnings release, net profit stood at Rs 3,627 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, which included a one-time gain of Rs 1,699 crore from the sale of its strategic investment in National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL).

The bank stated, "Excluding this one-off gain, YoY increase in Operating Profit and Net profit is 59% and 14% for Q2 FY27 respectively."

Operating profit stood at Rs 2,893 crore, compared with Rs 3,523 crore a year earlier. Excluding the exceptional gain, operating profit increased 59 per cent to Rs 1,824 crore.

The bank's core lending income also strengthened, with net interest income rising 29 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,228 crore from Rs 3,285 crore.

Net interest margin improved to 4.11 per cent from 3.71 per cent a year earlier, while the cost of deposits declined to 4.55 per cent.

Asset quality also improved, with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declining to 2.12 per cent from 2.65 per cent a year earlier, while net NPAs fell to 0.17 per cent from 0.21 per cent.

The bank stated, "The PCR is consistently above 99% since September 2023." Its provision coverage ratio, including technical write-offs, stood at 99.24 per cent.

Total deposits grew 17 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3.56 lakh crore, while net advances increased 18 per cent to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.

The results come amid the ongoing strategic disinvestment process in IDBI Bank, with the Finance Ministry issuing a clarification on Saturday concerning legislative developments related to the government's shareholding in the lender.

The latest earnings indicate stronger core banking performance and improving asset quality, despite the sharp decline in reported profit caused by last year's exceptional gain.

data.title: Bitcoin On Track For First Back-To-Back Losing Octobers In Over A Decade As ‘Downtober’ Continues
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin was down over 2% so far in October, putting it on track for its first back-to-back losing October in more than 10 years.
  • October has been one of Bitcoin's strongest months, averaging about 18% gains. 
  • Last year, Bitcoin hit its all-time high early in the month before an Oct. 10 crash sent it lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) was on track for its first consecutive October decline, with Bankless co-founder David Hoffman calling Friday “the third week of Downtober.”

October has long been one of Bitcoin's best months. Its average October return was about 18.3%, and its median is about 12.7%, according to CoinGlass data. Before last year, the month had ended lower only twice, in 2014 and 2018.

YearMonthly Returns In October
2026-2.48%
2025-3.69%
2024+10.76%
2023+28.52%
2022+5.56%
2021+39.93%
2020+27.7%
2019+10.17%
2018-3.83%
2017+47.81%
2016+14.71%

Source: Coinglass.

Last October started on a high. Bitcoin hit its all-time high of about $126,000 early in the month, before a crash on October 10 erased those gains. This year it has been different. The world's largest cryptocurrency was down over 2% so far this month. It also fell more than 3% last October. Bitcoin has not posted two red Octobers in a row in more than 10 years, with its highest gain in October being in 2017.

Bankless co-founders Hoffman and Ryan Sean Adams discussed that Bitcoin climbed into October from the $60,000s, rather than falling from a record. "The direction of travel is quite different," one of them said.

This Week's Slide

Bitcoin dipped to around $80,000 this week, its lowest level since September 18. It is down about 7% for the year. The selling had been heavier in altcoins, where Ethereum (ETH) fell about 7.5% over the week, the hosts said, while tokens like Solana (SOL), Zchas (ZEC), Hyperliquid (HYPE) and Near Protocol (NEAR) dropped another 10% after double-digit losses the week before.

'They Feel Sideways'

The hosts argued that a choppy market fits an early bull run. They pointed to 2023, when Bitcoin spent about seven months moving sideways and suffered two 17% pullbacks. Through that stretch, Bitcoin held above its 50-week moving average.

"So that's kind of the way early bull markets feel. They feel sideways," Adams said. Neither expected Bitcoin to fall below its low from a few months ago. "We have broken the back of the bear market," Adams added.

Bitcoin's monthly returns have swung widely this year. CoinGlass data showed it fell about 10% in January, 15% in February, and 20% in June, but gained about 25% in August.

data.title: Air India, Air India Express extend Saudi Arabia flight suspension until Oct 24 amid Houthi strikes: What airline said
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Air India and its subsidiary Air India Express have extended the suspension of services connecting Indian cities with Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam in Saudi Arabia until October 24, citing the prevailing security situation in West Asia following Houthi rebel strikes in the region.

The airline has also announced a one-time complimentary rescheduling facility for affected passengers, adding that tickets booked on or before October 15 for journeys scheduled between October 9 and 25 will be eligible for a free change of travel date, provided the revised journey takes place by November 10.

In a travel advisory, Air India said the extended suspension could disrupt passengers' travel arrangements and that the airlines were seeking to offer greater flexibility to those affected.

The statement read, "In view of the prevailing situation, Air India and Air India Express have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 24 October 2026. We understand that these disruptions may affect our guests' travel plans and are committed to providing as much flexibility as possible during this period."

"Guests holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before 15 October 2026, with travel dates between 9 October and 25 October 2026, are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change on their respective airline up to 10 November 2026. Guests who do not wish to rebook on the originally preferred sector for a future date may, instead, choose to rebook from an alternative station in the GCC region served by their respective airline, subject to availability," it added.

Affected passengers can also choose to travel to an alternative destination in West Asia, subject to the airline's applicable options. Air India customers can reschedule their journeys to or from Dubai or Doha, while Air India Express passengers can opt for Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Bahrain, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Salalah or Sharjah, the airline said.

However, passengers will have to arrange their own transport to the alternative departure point and ensure they meet the relevant visa and entry requirements, it said, further stating that those whose flights have been cancelled can also opt for a full refund if they decide not to travel.

"We continue to closely monitor the situation and will keep guests informed of any further updates. Our priority remains to support affected guests, minimise inconvenience, and help them continue their journeys with suitable travel options," Air India concluded.

IndiGo on Thursday extended the suspension of its flights to Saudi Arabian destinations until October 24.

Akasa Air announced that it would continue to suspend services to and from Riyadh until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21, citing the prevailing security situation in the Middle East.

The flight disruptions follow the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which has claimed 13 lives. The death toll rose after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national, who was injured in the incident, succumbed to his injuries.

Meanwhile, amid the escalation of the conflict, Yemen's internationally recognised government on Friday accused Houthi rebels of launching two missiles targeting Aden International Airport. According to the country's Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani, the missiles landed near a Yemenia Airways aircraft that was preparing to depart for Cairo.

data.title: Axis Bank's Q2 profit jumps 38% as provisions fall 52%, asset quality improves
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- Axis Bank reported a 38 per cent year-on-year jump in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, supported by a sharp 52 per cent decline in provisions and improving asset quality, even as its core operating profit grew at a slower pace.

According to the bank's earnings release and investor presentation filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday, provisions and contingencies fell to Rs 1,694 crore from Rs 3,547 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The decline in provisions helped boost profitability despite operating profit rising only 6 per cent to Rs 11,083 crore.

However, the year-ago quarter included a one-time standard asset provision of Rs 1,231 crore, which contributed to the sharp year-on-year decline in provisions.

The bank stated in its investor presentation that "GNPA, NNPA, slippages and credit costs improved YOY and QOQ."

Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declined to 1.16 per cent from 1.46 per cent a year earlier, while net NPAs improved to 0.35 per cent from 0.44 per cent.

Fresh loan slippages also fell to Rs 4,762 crore from Rs 5,696 crore in the year-ago quarter, indicating fewer loans turning bad.

The bank's annualised net credit cost declined to 0.45 per cent, down 28 basis points year-on-year.

Meanwhile, net interest income rose 12 per cent to Rs 15,371 crore, while net interest margin stood at 3.36 per cent.

The bank's earnings release highlighted "Robust growth in deposits at 21% YOY and 6% QOQ and advances at 23% YOY and 9% QOQ."

Total deposits reached Rs 14.52 lakh crore, while advances stood at Rs 13.74 lakh crore. Corporate lending grew 34 per cent year-on-year, outpacing retail loan growth of 16 per cent.

The results indicate that lower provisioning requirements and improving loan quality supported Axis Bank's earnings growth, alongside continued expansion in lending and deposits.

data.title: Deutsche Bank Nears Bitcoin Custody Launch As Crypto Push Expands Beyond Europe
data.description:
TL;DR: Deutsche Bank is preparing to introduce institutional digital asset custody services, initially targeting professional clients in Germany. The planned platform is part of a wider effort to connect cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets to established banking infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank is nearing the commercial launch of its institutional cryptocurrency custody business, another sign that major European lenders increasingly regard digital assets as part of mainstream financial services.

Comments reported on October 16 indicated that the German banking giant expects to begin serving institutional customers within weeks. Its offering is intended to support assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum, using technology developed with Swiss digital asset infrastructure company Taurus.

This is not a new retail cryptocurrency trading app. The initial market consists of businesses and professional investors with demanding custody and compliance requirements.

Why Banks Are Entering Custody

Holding cryptocurrency for institutional clients involves more than storing private keys. Banks must address asset segregation, operational controls, reporting, insurance arrangements and regulators’ expectations.

The service would allow eligible institutions to interact with digital assets through a familiar banking relationship rather than exclusively relying on specialised cryptocurrency companies.

Traditional finance is already developing related infrastructure. Projects involving blockchain settlement and tokenized deposits illustrate how established financial businesses are adapting their systems.

The Longer-Term Opportunity

Deutsche Bank has also discussed tokenized deposits, digital securities and possible expansion into Asian financial centres in 2027.

These ambitions remain subject to regulatory approvals and operating arrangements. A planned launch should not be confused with an already operating global service.

Nevertheless, the direction is clear. Rather than merely offering clients exposure to cryptocurrency prices, traditional banks increasingly want to provide the infrastructure through which digital assets are held, transferred and managed.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Yes Bank Q2 Results: Low provisions, high other income aid profits; Asset quality stable
data.description:
Mumbai-based private lender Yes Bank Ltd. reported September quarter results on Saturday, October 17, which were higher on a year-on-year basis on the profitability and core income front.

Yes Bank's Net Interest Income (NII) or core income that it earned, grew by 22.7% during the quarter to ₹2,822.5 crore, compared to ₹2,301 crore it reported during the same quarter last year.

Net profit for the period stood at ₹1,080 crore. That's a 65% growth compared to the year-ago period and also means that the bank has not taken into account any potential losses arising from the AT-1 bond issue, which led to the stock declining nearly 20% across Thursday and Friday.

Asset quality for the private lender remained stable with Gross NPA at 1.2% from 1.3% in June, while Net NPA remaining unchanged at 0.2% from 0.2% in the previous quarter. In absolute terms, Yes Bank's Gross NPA stood at ₹3,875 crore, while its Net NPA stood at ₹757 crore. This is in comparison to the ₹3,704 crore and ₹677 crore it reported respectively during the previous quarter.

Provisions for the quarter declined to ₹317.4 crore from ₹395 crore in June, while other income increased to ₹1,881.5 crore from ₹1,644.3 crore last year. Both contributed to the growth in the bank's profitability.

Based on its business update reported earlier this month, Yes Bank's loans and advances had grown by 23.8% on a year-on-year basis to ₹3.09 lakh crore, while deposits saw growth of 19.5% to ₹3.54 lakh crore from ₹2.96 lakh crore earlier.

CASA Ratio stood at 33.7% from 30% in the year-ago period. Normalized for the FCNR (B) inflows, Yes Bank's loan growth stood at 17.7% and deposit growth stood at 13.2% from last year.

Yes Bank has been in the news through Thursday and Friday after the Supreme Court decided to set aside the write-off of its Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth over ₹8,400 crore.

Sources had told CNBC-TV18 exclusively that the lender could recognize the potential ₹5,300 crore to ₹5,400 crore earnings hit during the ongoing quarter itself, or push it to the December quarter, but not later than that.

The write-off had taken place during the RBI-led reconstruction of Yes Bank, when the lender was facing a severe financial crisis. The rescue involved capital support from State Bank of India and other lenders, while the AT-1 bonds were written down to zero.

Shares of Yes Bank had ended at the day's low on Friday as well, declining 3.4% to end at ₹17.5. This follows a 14.5% drop on Thursday after the Supreme Court judgment.

data.title: Insurance stocks, TransUnion among winners; Banks, IREN in losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF advanced 1.44% from the prior week to close at $55.52.

Among megacap financial stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank was a notable gainer, adding 4.60% week-over-week to $120.39.

TD Bank was among the nine largest U.S. banks engaged in the so-called "debanking" activity, according to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's recent report.

The stock lost 0.27% on the day, but was rising for the remainder of the week.

Mastercard (+4.80% W/W to $617.42) and Visa (+4.45% W/W to $402.61) were the other major gainers. The two stocks have been gaining since the launch of Open USD stablecoin last month.

Bank of America led the decliners, having posted its worst day since April 2025 on Wednesday. The stock fell 5.69% week-over-week to $51.23.

The stock plunged after the U.S. Department of the Treasury imposed over $1.21B in penalties against the lender over anti-money laundering and sanctions laws violations. The regulatory fine impacted the bank's third-quarter profit.

Morgan Stanley's Q3 earnings exceeded expectations despite a weakness in fixed income and investment management. However, the stock underperformed with a 4.97% decline to $180.57.

Citigroup followed with a 4.15% decrease to $124.26. Q3 earnings beat analyst estimates but saw sequential declines across investment banking, trading, and firm-wide profitability.

The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index underperformed the broader markets, with investors split on how to read Q3 bank earnings, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

"One camp sees positive net interest income outlooks and strong returns and capital and consumer spend. The other sees rising deposits costs and [accumulated other comprehensive income] eating buybacks and concerns on lending standards and credit sustainability," said Truist Securities analyst Brian Foran.

Among largecap stocks, TransUnion topped the advancers with a 13.13% addition to $74.08. The week saw TransUnion strike a deal with Bankrate to power more personalized credit offers for millions of consumers.

Additionally, a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.

IREN (-23.30% W/W to $26.99) was the biggest loser despite the crypto miner-turned-AI server agreeing on a multiyear cloud deal with Anthropic.

data.title: Notable analyst calls: Salesforce, Walmart and Lockheed Martin gain analyst support as tech downgrades mount
data.description:
Wall Street analysts issued a fresh round of upgrades and downgrades last week, with shifting views on AI’s impact on software, hardware makers’ growth prospects, and resilience to inflation. Salesforce and Walmart drew upgrades, while Adobe and several technology hardware stocks faced downgrades.

Salesforce upgraded by Bank of America on enterprise AI outlook

Salesforce (CRM) was upgraded to Buy from Underperform by Bank of America on October 12, with the brokerage raising its price target to $285 from $160. The firm said large enterprises are unlikely to replace software platforms that house their business logic, data, workflows and compliance frameworks as they adopt AI. Instead, AI adoption could deepen reliance on these systems.

The $285 price target values Salesforce  at 16 times its expected free cash flow for 2027, up from 9 times previously and above the peer average of 15 times. The brokerage cited easing concerns about AI-driven disruption, the company's AI strategy, strong free cash flow generation and the potential for revenue growth to accelerate.

Barclays downgrades Dell, HPE and NetApp as AI growth concerns mount

Dell Technologies (DELL), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and NetApp (NTAP) were downgraded to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 14. Analyst Tim Long lowered Dell's price target to $574 from $603 and HPE's to $77 from $83, while maintaining NetApp's target at $219.

Barclays adopted a more cautious view of IT hardware companies exposed to enterprise spending, citing elevated valuations, revenue gains supported by higher memory prices and a lack of a meaningful AI-driven growth inflection.

HubSpot and monday.com downgraded by Barclays on delayed AI benefits

HubSpot (HUBS) and monday.com (MNDY) were downgraded to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 12, as the brokerage said AI-related benefits could take longer to materialize than previously expected.

Barclays maintained its price target of $240 for HubSpot and $100 for monday.com . For HubSpot , the firm said its bullish thesis had relied on AI usage accelerating growth, but customer caution during the AI transition could delay that improvement. For monday.com , analyst Raimo Lenschow said AI monetization was gaining traction but remained in its early stages, with AI ARR accounting for only 1% of total ARR and not yet offsetting a slowdown in core growth.

Deutsche Bank upgrades Walmart as inflation bolsters value proposition

Walmart was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Deutsche Bank on October 15, with analyst Krisztina Katai raising the price target to $136 from $113. The brokerage said persistent inflation could strengthen Walmart’s value proposition and accelerate market-share gains as consumers seek lower prices.

Deutsche Bank expects margin growth from advertising, marketplace, and membership, alongside automation gains. Strong food market-share gains and e-commerce momentum also support its improved 2027 outlook.

GoDaddy downgraded by RBC as AI reshapes the web

GoDaddy (GDDY) was downgraded to Sector Perform from Outperform by RBC Capital Markets on October 12. Analyst Brad Erickson maintained his $95 price target, citing the potential impact of AI agents on the company's traditional domain, website-building and digital-commerce businesses.

RBC said the internet was shifting from static, publisher-driven pages toward AI agents that deliver results based on user intent. The brokerage also cited GoDaddy's 38% rebound from its June low, saying the rally left less room for further valuation expansion.

MongoDB stays bullish as Needham and BofA reaffirm Buy ratings

MongoDB (MDB) rose more than 6% on October 13 after Needham and Bank of America reiterated their Buy ratings on the database software company. Needham maintained its price target at $430, while BofA kept its target at $540.

Needham analyst Mike Cikos said discussions following MongoDB's Investor Day reinforced the firm's confidence in the company's go-to-market strategy, platform cross-selling opportunities, and potential to expand adoption among large customers. Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda said MongoDB's JSON document database remains differentiated for enterprise digital modernization and AI workloads, supporting the firm's long-term growth outlook.

Wells Fargo double downgrades Adobe, upgrades Tyler Technologies

Adobe (ADBE) was downgraded to Underweight from Overweight by Wells Fargo on October 12, with analyst Michael Turrin cutting the price target to $225 from $270. The firm cited slowing organic growth, rising AI competition and execution risks amid a management transition.

In contrast, Wells Fargo upgraded Tyler Technologies (TYL) to Overweight from Equal Weight and raised its price target to $400 from $335, citing fading booking headwinds and scope for a recovery in 2027.

Well Fargo also raised its price targets on ServiceNow (NOW) to $190 from $175, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) to $525 from $475, and CrowdStrike (CRWD) to $300 from $235. It cut its target on Figma (FIG) to $30 from $34.

Vertical Research upgrades Lockheed Martin on missile demand

Lockheed Martin was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Vertical Research on October 14, with analyst Robert Stallard setting a $600 price target. Stallard expects the company’s missile business to grow about 11% annually through the end of the decade, citing demand for missile replenishment despite uncertainty over the U.S. defense budget.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: CoreWeave, TSMC, Anthropic in focus
data.description:
Technology stocks slumped this week, with chipmakers and AI infrastructure providers leading losses as investors questioned the returns on heavy AI investments.

The Nasdaq Composite also came under pressure, falling more than 4% for the week, while the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) fell 7.20% over the week, reflecting broad weakness across the technology sector.

The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Fair Isaac +13.91%
  • Cognizant Technology Solutions +9.56%
  • Tyler Technologies +8.55%
  • Accenture +8.05%
  • Gartner +6.66%

Top Losers:

  • Ciena -25.14%
  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise -25.08%
  • Coherent -24.62%
  • Super Micro Computer -24.44%
  • Lumentum -24.21%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

CoreWeave sell-off puts AI infrastructure financing under scrutiny

CoreWeave shares plunged 12.80% on Friday as investors questioned the cost of expanding AI data centers. The sell-off spread to Nebius and IREN amid concerns about borrowing costs and capital requirements.

CoreWeave's debt and lease obligations totaled approximately $52B at the end of June, highlighting the financial burden of its AI infrastructure expansion.

TSMC outlook signals resilient AI chip demand

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing forecasted fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3B to $54.3B, above analysts' consensus of $50.48B, providing fresh evidence of resilient semiconductor demand.

Third-quarter high-performance computing revenue rose 22% quarter over quarter. Management said AI accelerator revenue growth could exceed its previous mid-to-high-50% CAGR forecast for 2024–2029, signaling continued demand despite the broader technology sell-off.

Anthropic IPO valuation expectations cool as growth slows

Anthropic's anticipated initial public offering faces greater valuation scrutiny as investors assess its growth trajectory and AI development costs.

Reuters reported that some investors were discussing a potential valuation of around $1.5T, below earlier expectations of approximately $2T.

The AI company reportedly generated $16.8B in third-quarter revenue, up 45% sequentially, and was profitable on an adjusted basis. However, the slower growth rate disappointed some investors after revenue more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6B in the second quarter.

The valuation discussions remain preliminary and do not represent confirmed IPO pricing.

AI spending pressures hyperscaler cash flow

Bank of America Global Research expects Microsoft to be the only major hyperscaler among its comparison group not to enter negative free cash flow territory over the next 12 months.

Amazon , Alphabet , Oracle , and Meta Platforms are projected to face negative free cash flow as AI infrastructure investment continues. The firm expects cash generation to recover by the second half of 2027, assuming AI revenue accelerates and capital expenditure growth slows.

Bank of America sees memory-stock sell-off diverging from fundamentals

Bank of America analysts said the recent pullback in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics may reflect fears of an AI spending slowdown rather than weakening memory fundamentals. Investors have worried about borrowing costs for AI cloud providers, potential Chinese supply growth, and the sustainability of demand.

BofA, however, expects memory prices, sales, and margins to remain strong through 2028. The divergence highlights uncertainty around the memory cycle: shares have come under pressure even as some forecasts point to continued demand and earnings strength.

Meta expands open AI model push with Muse Spark Open

Meta Platforms released Muse Spark Open, an AI model designed for coding and complex tasks. It has 816B parameters, with 42B active during use, and its weights are available to developers. The model can run locally on suitably configured Apple Mac Studio computers, expanding Meta's open-model offering.

data.title: Hungary PM Magyar to present 2027 budget in parliament on Monday
data.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar will present the 2027 budget in parliament on Monday, targeting savings in public operating expenditure and planning for a surge in European Union-funded investments, he said on Saturday.

The 2027 budget is seen as a key credibility test for Magyar as he tried to curb the deficit to below the EU's 3% target ceiling while still honouring the pledges that helped secure his landslide election win over Viktor Orban in April.

Deutsche Bank said overseas investors had poured $13.5 billion into the local bond market year-to-date as of late September, betting heavily on centre-right Magyar's pledge to meet euro entry conditions by 2030.

"The TISZA government will spend more resources on those who have lost out in recent years, as well as on families, Hungarian businesses, pensioners, education and healthcare," Magyar said in a Facebook post.

"The 2027 budget will save money on the operation of the state and redirect funds from billionaires and polluting companies to the millions who have so far been left behind."

Magyar said billions of euros worth of European Union funding released after the rollback of Orban-era reforms seen as harming democracy would be used to launch "unprecedented" investments in housing, transport and water management.

Magyar's euro pledge has triggered a rally in Hungary's forint , which helped drive inflation sharply below the central bank's target. Market expectations for cuts in the deficit have bolstered government bonds.

Economists polled by Reuters see the deficit falling to 5.3% of output in 2027, compared with the government's 7.5% target for 2026. Analysts see Hungary joining the euro in 2032 or 2033.

data.title: Bank of Canada sees sharply higher inflation outlook as oil surges, Macklem says
data.description:
By Promit Mukherjee

The Bank of Canada expects to raise its quarterly inflation forecast significantly this month owing to persistently high crude oil and petroleum product prices, Governor Tiff Macklem said on Saturday.

New quarterly inflation and growth forecasts will feed into the BoC's rate decision on October 28.

"With the (Middle East) conflict ongoing, shipments still curtailed and refinery capacity damage, the risk that inflation broadens and becomes more persistent has gone up," Macklem told journalists on a conference call from Bangkok.

"Our beacon is our 2% inflation target, and we are committed to keeping inflation close to target over time. We are prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed."

Money market expectations of an increase in rates have been growing in the last few months but, as of Saturday, markets were not pricing in any change on October 28 or at the bank's last monetary policy decision of the year in December.

However, they are pricing in increases of 100 basis points over the course of next year. (0#CADIRPR)

Macklem said the global economy had shown resilience despite the conflict in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war, but that resilience was being tested by higher costs and tighter financial conditions.

He said governments also had less fiscal room to maneuver and needed to adjust their policies to rebuild that capacity.

For central bankers, the main concern is to ascertain whether higher oil and product prices will spill over into the broader economy.

Speaking about the decision to be made on October 28, Macklem said: "The question we are going to be asking ourselves is, 'Is inflation likely to come back down towards our target on its own, or are we going to have to raise interest rates to influence the path, nudge the path for inflation back towards the target?'."

data.title: Reliance Jio IPO GMP today: Listing-day jackpot or long-term bet? How should investors play Mukesh Ambani's mega IPO?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The countdown to India's largest initial public offering (IPO) has begun. Jio Platforms IPO, backed by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries Limited, is garnering heightened investors' interest ahead of the opening of its subscription period. Jio IPO's latest grey market premium (GMP) hints at 19.75% listing gains.

Jio Platforms is offering 27 crore new equity shares in the price band of between Rs.1,065 and Rs.1,119 per share to investors. Which makes the Jio IPO a Rs.30,213 crore issuance at the upper end of the price band. As all eyes are now on India's biggest ever IPO, let's understand whether the Jio IPO will be more than a listing day jackpot and long-term bet for investors.

Jio Platforms latest IPO GMP was recorded at Rs.221 at 2:02 pm on Saturday, October 17, as per media reports. With an upper price band of Rs.1,119 per share, the estimated listing price for the Jio Platforms IPO is Rs.1,340 (which is the sum of the upper price band and latest IPO GMP today). Considering the grey market premium of Jio Platforms IPO, the issue is likely to see 19.75% listing gain.

Investors must note that the grey market premium indicates demand for an issue in the unregulated market and is not an accurate representation of an IPO's listing day performance.

The IPO is a book-build issue of Rs.30,213 crores and an entirely fresh issue of 27 crore shares of Rs.30,213 crore. The IPO has fixed issue price band at Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 per share. The lot size for an application is 12 shares. The minimum amount a retail investor can put in Jio IPO is Rs.13,428 for 12 shares.

The IPO will open for subscriptions on October 21, 2026. The issue will close for subscription on October 23, 2026. The IPO allotment will likely be finalised for the Jio IPO on October 26, 2026. The IPO is expected to list on NSE and BSE on October 28, 2026.

Jio Platforms is well positioned to capitalise on India's growing digital economy, which is supported by its customer base of 533.3 million, extensive pan-India connectivity and approximately 60% share of wireless data traffic.

Jio IPO's valuation looks relatively attractive compared to Bharti Airtel's price to earnings ratio (P/E), according to Kantilal Chhaganlal brokerage, which goves 'Subscribe' rating for long-term perspective.

"At the Upper Price Band of Rs.1,119 and FY2026 P/E of 33.3x, the valuation appears relatively attractive compared with Bharti Airtel's stated P/E of 40.71x, while regulatory changes, competitive pressures and high capital expenditure remain key risks, Jio's market leadership, profitability and structural growth opportunities support giving Long Term Positive outlook . Hence, We Recommend Investor to Subscribe issue from Long Term Prospective," noted the brokerage in its report.

Jio Platforms Limited is a leading technology platform combining panIndia digital connectivity with digital services to drive India's digital transformation.

Its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited has a 533.3 million customer base, as of June 30, 2026. Jio is not just a dominant player in the telecom industry but also continues to strengthen its technological capabilities.

data.title: Hurricane Trudy threatens western Mexico with heavy rain, coastal flooding
data.description:
Hurricane Trudy maintained its strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen further before beginning to weaken on Sunday.

The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 190 miles (305 km) south-southeast of Manzanillo early on Saturday, with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph).

The hurricane was moving at about 8 mph (13 kph) and was forecast to approach southwestern and west-central Mexico later on Saturday before passing near the coast overnight into Sunday.

Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region during the day, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch.

Trudy is forecast to bring four to eight inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with isolated totals of around 15 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC.

Outer rain bands could produce two to four inches of rain, with isolated totals of around six inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said.

The NHC also warned of possible coastal flooding from storm surge in areas exposed to onshore winds, accompanied by large and destructive waves.

Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico's southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country's west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

data.title: HDFC Bank's Q2 profit growth limited to 4.7% as treasury gains plunge 67%
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- HDFC Bank reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, as a sharp 67 per cent decline in treasury trading gains weighed on earnings despite stronger income from its core lending business.

According to the bank's earnings release filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday, treasury trading gains fell to Rs 780 crore from Rs 2,390 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The decline limited overall profit growth even as net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased by 9.7 per cent.

Highlighting the impact, the bank stated, "PAT, excluding treasury trading gains, grew by approximately 12.6% over the quarter ended September 30, 2025."

Net interest income rose to Rs 34,620 crore from Rs 31,550 crore a year earlier, supported by continued expansion in lending.

The bank said, "Net interest margin was at 3.16% on total assets, and 3.32% based on interest earning assets."

Net revenue increased to Rs 48,450 crore from Rs 45,900 crore, while fee and commission income rose to Rs 9,690 crore from Rs 8,840 crore.

Operating expenses stood at Rs 18,970 crore, while provisions and contingencies were Rs 3,570 crore during the quarter.

Despite pressure on earnings, asset quality improved.

"Gross non-performing assets were at 1.11% of gross advances as on September 30, 2026," the bank said, compared with 1.17 per cent in the preceding quarter and 1.24 per cent a year earlier.

Net NPAs stood at 0.37 per cent.

Total deposits grew 18.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 33.27 lakh crore, while gross advances increased 16.3 per cent to Rs 32.20 lakh crore.

The results highlight stronger core banking operations and improving asset quality, even as lower treasury gains restricted overall profitability.

data.title: HDFC Bank sees margins turning upwards from next quarter, says Sashidhar Jagdishan
data.description:
HDFC Bank expects its margins to recover from next quarter as the interest rate trajectory turns upwards, outgoing managing director and chief executive officer Sashidhar Jagdishan said, offering a positive outlook after the lender reported its lowest-ever net interest margin in the September quarter.

Jagdishan told CNBC-TV18 that margins had come under pressure during the quarter but expected the trend to change as the interest rate trajectory turned upwards. With a large part of the bank’s loan book linked to external benchmarks, he expects net interest margins (NIMs) to move higher.

The comments come as pressure on margins remains a key concern for investors, even as the bank reported healthy growth in its core lending business. HDFC Bank’s NIM declined to 3.16% in the September quarter, compared with 3.26% in the June quarter.

During the earnings call, Jagdishan said the bank’s topline growth had been healthy and expressed confidence in the resilience of its asset quality, which he expects to remain strong.

HDFC Bank reported a net profit of ₹19,510 crore for the September quarter, up 4.7% year-on-year and in line with estimates. Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 9.7% year-on-year to ₹34,620 crore. Deposits grew 18.8%, while the gross non-performing asset ratio stood at 1.11%.

The bank’s treasury trading income, however, fell 67.4% year-on-year to ₹780 crore, compared with ₹2,390 crore in the year-ago quarter. Excluding treasury trading gains, net profit grew 12.6% year-on-year, against reported growth of 4.7%.

Jagdishan backs continuity as Anup Bagchi prepares to take charge

With Anup Bagchi set to take over as managing director and chief executive officer after Jagdishan’s term ends on October 26, the outgoing chief highlighted the depth of the bank’s leadership and the importance of institutional continuity.

Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Jagdishan said HDFC Bank was not dependent on any one individual, noting that experienced leaders, including Kaizad Bharucha and Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, had played important roles. He expressed confidence that the depth of the management team would help preserve the institution’s continuity and ethos.

Jagdishan described Bagchi as a seasoned financial services professional with 34 years of experience across banking and insurance. He said the incoming chief was well placed to lead a team of capable leaders and wished him well ahead of the transition.

Bagchi, in his comments to CNBC-TV18, highlighted the strength of the institution and its team, saying the organisation remained committed to the bank. He added that much of the clean-up work was behind the lender, although some more work remained.

data.title: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund cash falls to 9.77% after Rajeev Thakkar's 'single-digit' outlook: Where is the money going?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, the country's largest active mutual fund scheme by AUM, has stepped up its investment deployment, reducing its allocation to cash and related instruments over the past six months.

The fund's factsheets show that its combined allocation to cash, debt and money market instruments, and arbitrage positions fell to 9.77% in September 2026 from 18.94% in March, nearly halving over six months. The share also dropped by 1.81 percentage points from 11.58% in August 2026. Here's what investors need to know.

Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund's September 2026 factsheet reiterates its focus on identifying individual investment opportunities rather than making allocation decisions primarily on the basis of macroeconomic conditions.

"We continue to look at individual investments on their own merits and will not hesitate to invest if an opportunity looks attractive," the factsheet stated.

It added that the fund had about 9.77% in cash holdings, debt and money market instruments, and arbitrage positions that could be deployed into long-term investments at appropriate levels.

The March 2026 factsheet had reported the corresponding allocation at 18.94%, while the August factsheet put it at 11.58%. The successive declines indicate that the fund has been reducing its deployable reserves as investment opportunities emerge.

In his August 2026 communication to unitholders, Rajeev Thakkar, CIO - Equity and Director at PPFAS, said the fund was increasingly finding opportunities to invest.

"Cash levels peaked at about 25%. They are down to about 14%-15% in Flexi Cap. We are increasingly finding opportunities to buy, and one may look forward to single-digit cash levels in some time," Thakkar said.

He also said that holding cash during the preceding two years had not harmed investor returns and had helped at the margin during a sideways market.

The September allocation of 9.77% seems to be consistent with the direction indicated in his August remarks.

According to the September 2026 factsheet, Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund (Direct plan) has delivered a 17.76% return since its inception on 24 May 2013, outperforming the Nifty 500 TRI benchmark's 13.56% return.

Over three years, the fund returned 12.21%, against 9.50% for the benchmark. Its five-year return stood at 11.15%, compared with 9.04% for the index.

However, the fund underperformed over the 1-year period ended 30 September 2026, declining 3.54% against the benchmark's 2.03% fall.

The fund completely exited Great Eastern Shipping Company in September 2026 and did not add any new stock to its portfolio.

It increased its holdings in 13 existing positions. DLF saw the largest addition by quantity, with the fund adding 390.64 lakh shares. Its holding rose from 137.10 lakh shares in August to 527.73 lakh shares in September.

Petronet LNG, Indus Towers and Indraprastha Gas were among the other stocks in which the fund increased its holdings.

The fund did not reduce the quantity held in any stock during the month. Its holdings in major companies, including HDFC Bank, Power Grid, ITC, Coal India, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Infosys, remained unchanged.

The declining cash allocation and additions to existing positions suggest that the fund is deploying capital selectively rather than making broad changes across its portfolio.

data.title: Delhi Court Rejects Bail Plea Of Former Reliance Capital CFO Amit Bapna
data.description:
The court cited evidence of Bapna’s alleged role in corporate loan disbursements by RCFL and the bypassing of board sanctions at RHFL

A Delhi court has rejected the bail plea of Amit Bapna, former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Reliance Capital, in an alleged bank loan fraud-linked money laundering case. The court cited evidence indicating his alleged role in loan disbursements by Reliance Commercial Finance (RCFL) and the bypassing of sanctions imposed by the board of Reliance Home Finance (RHFL).

Special Judge Vishal Pahuja, in an order passed on Thursday, said the evidence gathered by the prosecution indicated Bapna’s alleged control over the affairs of RHFL and RCFL.

“The evidence gathered by the prosecution agency against the applicant/accused (Bapna) is overwhelming and indicates towards his overarching control over the affairs of RHFL and RCFL,” the court said.

The court said the evidence indicated that Bapna was aware of transactions carried out by the companies and allegedly intended to benefit companies belonging to the Reliance Anil Ambani Group.

According to the court, large sums were transferred under the guise of general corporate loans without adequate verification of the borrowers’ financial positions.

The court also referred to evidence suggesting that shell entities with negative net worth were incorporated and used as conduits to siphon off public money.

The prosecution complaint, or chargesheet, and accompanying documents further indicated that Bapna allegedly exercised decision-making powers in RCFL without authorisation and proceeded with corporate loan disbursements despite sanctions imposed by RHFL’s board of directors.

Court Rejects Parity Argument

The court rejected Bapna’s counsel’s argument that the Enforcement Directorate (ED) had not arrested other co-accused who were allegedly similarly placed.

It observed that Bapna held a higher position in the functioning of Reliance Capital, RHFL and RCFL than the other accused. According to the court, he was at the helm of affairs, issued instructions to other co-accused and had some of them reporting to him.

The court also rejected the argument that Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, another co-accused, was the principal decision-maker and architect of the alleged offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), while Bapna had merely followed his instructions.

It said that even if Jhunjhunwala was considered the principal architect of the transactions, Bapna, in his capacity as CFO, was allegedly equally and proactively involved.

Custody & Bail Considerations

The court said Bapna was not entitled to bail solely because he had spent more than five months in custody. It noted that the investigation was continuing and cited the alleged scale of the offence, Bapna’s position and the possibility of influencing witnesses or tampering with evidence.

The court also distinguished Bapna’s case from that of Jhunjhunwala, who had been granted bail by the Delhi High Court. Referring to the prosecution agency’s chargesheet, it noted that Jhunjhunwala had received bail on medical grounds rather than on the merits of the case.

Dismissing Bapna’s plea, the court concluded that the grounds cited by the defence did not justify granting him bail at this stage.

data.title: Former IAS Officer SCL Das Appointed FSIB Head For 3 Years
data.description:
The government appoints former IAS officer Subhas Chandra Lal Das to lead the Financial Services Institutions Bureau, alongside six part-time members representing banking, financial institutions and insurance

The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has appointed retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Subhas Chandra Lal Das as part-time chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) for a three-year term, strengthening the body responsible for recommending senior appointments across state-run financial institutions.

The appointment will take effect from the date of notification or until further orders, whichever is earlier. The government has also appointed six part-time members to the bureau. The appointments cover public sector banks, financial institutions and insurance companies, bringing together former banking executives, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials and insurance-sector leaders.

Six Members Appointed

The members representing public sector banks and financial institutions are Arijit Basu, former managing director of State Bank of India; Satish Kashinath Marathe, former director on the RBI Central Board; and Ramanathan Subramanian, former RBI executive director.

For public sector insurers, the government has appointed Siddhartha Mohanty, former chairman and managing director of Life Insurance Corporation of India; Neerja Kapur, former chairperson and managing director of New India Assurance Company; and T. L. Alamelu, former member of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI). All appointments carry a three-year tenure from the date of notification or until further orders.

Role Of FSIB

The FSIB recommends candidates for senior leadership positions in public sector banks, insurance companies and financial institutions, including NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM Bank and the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID). The bureau plays a key role in the government’s selection process for top management positions across state-owned financial institutions. The reconstitution brings banking, regulatory and insurance experience into the body overseeing recommendations for these leadership appointments.

data.title: Ujjivan SFB Profit Outlook Brightens As Loans Grow 32%, Secured Lending Expands
data.description:
Brokerage Elara Securities retains its Buy rating with an Rs 87 target price, implying 38% upside, as improving asset quality and lower credit costs support earnings prospects

Ujjivan Small Finance Bank reported a sharp rise in second-quarter FY27 profit, supported by strong revenue momentum, loan growth and lower credit costs, according to an Elara Securities report dated 17 October 2026. The brokerage retained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 87, implying 38 per cent upside from its closing price of Rs 63 on 16 October. Net interest margin (NIM) declined by around 10 basis points sequentially to 8.4 per cent, reflecting a shift towards secured lending.

Elara expects the margin to ease further to about 8.3 per cent in the second half of FY27. The cost of funds stood at 6.9 per cent, but the brokerage flagged the possibility of a roughly 10-basis-point increase in the third quarter as the benefit from deposit repricing fades and higher repo-rate costs flow through. Loan growth remained strong at 32.4 per cent year-on-year, while deposits increased 29.2 per cent. The bank’s expanding secured portfolio and improving asset quality underpin Elara’s positive outlook, although deposit pricing and insurance commission regulations remain key risks.

Secured Lending Expands

Growth was broad-based across lending segments. Housing loans grew around 23.7 per cent year-on-year, micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) loans increased 43.5 per cent, and gold loans rose 209 per cent. Secured loans accounted for around 52 per cent of the portfolio, with the bank targeting a 56 per cent share by the end of FY27.

The bank added 66 branches during the quarter, taking its total network to 880. Operating expenses rose 11.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter and 26.1 per cent year-on-year, reflecting branch expansion and investment in its operating capacity. Management expects microfinance growth of 12–14 per cent for FY27. Elara noted that joint-liability group and individual lending each grew around 3 per cent sequentially.

Credit Costs Improve

Calculated credit costs declined by around 30 basis points sequentially to 0.95 per cent. Slippages stood at approximately Rs 180 crore, compared with Rs 170 crore in the previous quarter, while the slippage ratio remained around 1.6 per cent. Elara expects credit costs to remain near the bank’s full-year guidance of about 1 per cent, supported by better collections and lower provisions. The brokerage said the bank’s transition towards secured lending, alongside stabilisation in its microfinance and unsecured portfolio, could support a return on assets above 2 per cent in FY27.

It estimates return on assets of 2.3 per cent in FY27 and 2.2 per cent in FY28, with return on equity at 19 per cent and 18 per cent, respectively. Potential caps on insurance commissions proposed by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India could reduce FY28 return on assets by 10–20 basis points, Elara warned. Deposit pricing, the ability to raise the current account and savings account (CASA) ratio, and drought-related risks in Karnataka and Maharashtra also remain monitorable.
